# The GEO Stack: From llms.txt to Entity Graph

<callout icon="◈" color="blue_bg">
	**Working boundary.** The GEO Stack is Mason Nguyen's working map for maintaining a legible public source system. It is not an industry standard, a required protocol, or a claim that one layer makes a model retrieve or cite a page.
</callout>

## The stack is a maintenance map, not a visibility recipe

The stack organizes six connected layers: public source material, technical access, structured data, entity references, optional supplemental inventories, and maintenance records. The goal is to make an answer attributable and inspectable for people first, while avoiding the claim that a given platform outcome can be engineered.

Google says its AI Search features use the same foundational SEO practices as Search more broadly. It states that pages need Search eligibility, but that crawling, indexing, and serving are not guaranteed. [Google AI features guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)

## Layer 1: Public source material

The page itself carries the substantive answer, the author, the source links, the scope, and the date. The work must exist in readable main content before any markup or inventory can clarify it. Original research, a defined method, and a direct answer are more durable than a stack of labels.

## Layer 2: Technical access

Canonical URLs, crawl controls, internal links, readable HTML, a sitemap, and a usable page experience form the access layer. This is preparation for discovery, not proof that any system will crawl or serve a page.

## Layer 3: Structured data

Structured data can provide explicit clues about the meaning of visible page content. Google says markup should describe the page it appears on; complete and accurate properties matter more than a large or speculative graph. [Google structured data guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)

## Layer 4: Entity references

An entity record connects a declared person or organization to truthful references that help a reader disambiguate identity. Schema.org defines `sameAs` as a URL that unambiguously indicates an item's identity. It should not be used to claim equivalence where the relationship is uncertain. [Schema.org sameAs](https://schema.org/sameAs)

Google says Organization structured data can help it understand administrative details and disambiguate organizations, while recommending relevant properties rather than a boilerplate list. [Google Organization structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization)

Wikidata is one possible external structured-data ecosystem. Its records are collaborative, source-linked, and maintained by an editing community. A Wikidata item is not automatically appropriate for every project, and it should never be treated as an automatic authority credential. [Wikidata introduction](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Introduction)

## Layer 5: Supplemental inventory

An `llms.txt` file can be a maintained orientation document for people or systems that choose to use it. For Google generative Search, however, Google says `llms.txt` and similar AI text files are not used and do not improve visibility or rankings. [Google generative AI optimization guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)

The appropriate question is therefore not “Does this file rank us?” but “Is this inventory accurate, useful, and maintained for its actual audience?”

## Layer 6: Maintenance record

A public record needs source ownership, dates, revision notes, and documented observations. Search Console, analytics, and answer-engine samples can help a team observe what changed. They cannot prove a single cause for a mention, click, or business outcome.

## Recommended working order

1. Build the underlying source page and its evidence.
2. Make it technically accessible and internally connected.
3. Add structured data that matches the visible page.
4. Maintain truthful identity references where they are useful.
5. Publish optional inventories only when they serve a real user or system.
6. Record changes and observations without claiming causality beyond the evidence.
